registry.name: Registry
registry.description: Parties, items and companies: the base of the other modules.

warehouse.name: Warehouse
warehouse.description: Warehouses, movements, stock and reorder levels.

orders.name: Orders
orders.description: Customer and supplier orders, with reservation and fulfilment.

invoicing.name: Invoicing
invoicing.description: Invoices, credit notes, due dates and payments.

modules.neededBy: Needed by {{modules}}: switch that off first
modules.disableDescription: The data of {{module}} stays, and shows again if the module is switched back on. The people of {{tenant}} will no longer see its pages.

tenants.title: Customers
tenants.description: The customers using Mercurio. Here you create them and govern their modules, administrators and status; their working data stays theirs.

create.title: New customer
create.description: The customer starts with its first company, the chosen modules and its first administrator. Other companies, warehouses and colleagues are added by the administrator afterwards.
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: As people see it, for example “Verdi Group”.
create.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Used by commands and logs: it never changes after creation.
create.adminNameHint: Ignored if the person already has a Mercurio account.
create.existing: {{email}} already has a Mercurio account: they sign in as usual and will find {{tenant}} among their customers.

tenant.name: Name
tenant.companiesHint: The letterhead (address, IBAN, logo) is completed by the customer's administrator, from the Companies page.
tenant.otherPeople_one: {{count}} other person works for the customer.
tenant.otherPeople_other: {{count}} other people work for the customer.
tenant.noOtherPeople: Nobody else works for the customer.
tenant.never: Has not used the customer yet
tenant.promoteDescription: This person already works for the customer with the role “{{role}}”. They will become an administrator, with access to every company.
tenant.existingAdmin: {{email}} already has a Mercurio account: they sign in as usual.
tenant.suspendHint: A suspended customer cannot work until you reactivate it. The data stays.
tenant.reactivateHint: The customer is suspended: its people cannot work.
tenant.suspendDescription: The people of {{tenant}} will not be able to work until you reactivate it. The data stays.
tenant.historyHint: What operators did on this customer.
tenant.addCompanyHint: The same rules as the customer's administrator: the VAT number is unique within the customer.
tenant.companyAdded: {{name}} added. Administrators see it at once; people with a list of companies get it from the People page.

recovery.title: Account recovery
recovery.description: For people who activated their account and lost their phone or recovery codes. Look the person up by exact email and check which customers they work for before issuing the code.
recovery.emailHint: The exact address: parts of an email are not searched.
recovery.worksForHint: The administrators of these customers will see the recovery in their Activity, without the reason.
recovery.confirmDescription: The person's open sessions close now. When they use the code they lose their password, authenticator app and recovery codes, and set them up again. The code expires in 24 hours.
recovery.reasonHint: The person reads it in their account; it does not reach the customers.

blocked.SELF: This is your account: another operator does the recovery.
blocked.IS_OPERATOR: This is a platform operator: an operator is not recovered from the browser. From the terminal: issue-code --email {{email}}
blocked.NOT_ACTIVATED: The account is not activated yet: it needs an activation code, which their administrator issues from the People page (or you from the customer's page, for an administrator).
blocked.NO_MEMBERSHIP: Works for no customer: nobody would see the recovery. Add them to a customer first.

operators.title: Operators
operators.description: The people who run the platform, with the same powers. Adding and revoking ask for a new code of your authenticator app.
operators.name: Name
operators.terminalHint: An operator who activated their account and lost the authenticator app is recovered from the terminal (issue-code): an operator is never recovered from the browser.
operators.addDescription: They will reach the whole platform area: customers, recoveries and operators.
operators.nameHint: Needed only if the email has no Mercurio account yet.
operators.confirmExisting: This person already works for: {{tenants}}. Besides their work they will reach the platform area.
operators.grantedExisting: {{email}} already has a Mercurio account: they are now an operator and sign in as usual.
operators.revokeDescription: From their next request they no longer reach the platform area. The grant stays in the history.
operators.closeSessionsHint: For an account you believe compromised. Otherwise the person keeps working for their customers.
